$operator.summary: Named model configurations. Each configuration maps every checked-in Cursor persona to the model that should execute it.
$operator.note: This file carries the recommended defaults a release can update. Put per-checkout preferences (active_config, model overrides) in the untracked config_overrides.json, which merges over this file. After changing either, run ./.pancreator/bin/pan models --sync. New runs snapshot the active mapping so later config edits do not change an in-flight run.

balanced.summary: Balance of focused coding, strong review, and frontier planning.

advanced.summary: Higher-reasoning coding and QA for complex or high-risk work.

ultra.summary: Extreme configuration for the most demanding tasks.

auto.summary: Cursor-managed routing except for the bounded coding workhorse.

$operator.summary: Named profiles controlling how heavily the operator gates each workflow stage. Select one per run with ./bin/pan init --involvement <profile>; omitting the flag uses active.
$operator.note: gates maps a stage slug (or * for every stage) to the gate that stage uses for the run. contracts names run-wide contracts the run abides by. Runs snapshot the resolved profile, so later edits here do not change an in-flight run. Inspect available profiles with ./bin/pan involvement.

standard.summary: Workflow-declared gates, unchanged. The operator ratifies the plan and approves release preparation.

hands-off.summary: Minimum interruption. The supervisor ratifies the plan instead of the operator; release preparation still stops for explicit operator approval.

technical-director.summary: The operator refines the technical plan with its author before implementation and responds to the independent review before the run continues.

high-touch.summary: Every stage stops for explicit operator approval, and the technical-director refinement contract is active.

long-horizon.summary: Runs independently between preflight and post-run with bounded away-mode decisions; release preparation and every correctness boundary remain unchanged. waive-gate is allowed so a cost- or wall-time-backed criterion never stops a task; the decision budget is sized for a multi-hour run.

$operator.summary: Named verification levels controlling which repository-check profile each shell gate runs. Select one per run with ./bin/pan init --verification <level>; omitting the flag uses active.
$operator.note: Built-in levels: minimal (static and fast gate the implement and remediate loops; no gate runs full, including the ship release gate), light (static and fast gate the implement and remediate loops; the full profile runs only as the ship release gate when the run enters ship, a failure routes to remediate and returns to ship, at most twice before the operator decides), thorough (alias of light kept for existing snapshots). No verify or remediate gate runs full. Agents iterate on the impacted profile plus their added tests, run the fast profile once each as final validation, and never run full. The full profile is never baselined before implementation. Operator-declared levels here merge over the built-ins. Runs snapshot the resolved level. Change an in-flight run with ./bin/pan verification <run-id> set <level>. Inspect levels with ./bin/pan verification.
